decisions.reason: False positive: the product explicitly uses the n coordinates 1,...,n of a finite channel word, not an infinite real sequence indexed by all natural numbers. The Definition of def-sequence concerns functions N to R; it does not impose zero-based coordinates on finite alphabet products. There are exactly n factors, and summing over all output words yields the product of n row sums, equal to one (also for the empty product at n=0). No off-by-one or normalization defect exists.

At n=0 and positive message sizes, empty histories and a decoder on the singleton empty output word exist, but n^{-1} ln M_j is undefined. Step 2.1 therefore asserts false well-definedness on an unexcluded case. The repair explicitly requires integer n>=1 and nonempty finite message sets; the proof now uses these hypotheses for finite rates. Explicit encoder indices and empty-history notation preserve causal feedback, and achievability explicitly uses n tending to infinity.
